note: A list whose members are only known at runtime (issue #25). 2026-11-13: tried, not only read. A program declared with argenv 0.3.2 cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor more positionals than it names: a list needs a closed set of tokens, and only a list repeats. It is one need with three faces - snapall's --only declared as plain text (October, where this issue came from); an id typed from memory and refused three times in ocoeco's form (this week); and ocoeco's own --gathers, move TABLE ID..., and note --set, which cannot be declared at all. The three options in the issue ask how to permit free values; what the week showed is that the question is where values come from: declared (a closed set), asked (known only at runtime, and the program can tell them), or free (anything). 2026-11-13: designed (decision 2026-11-13-where-a-value-comes-from), prior art recorded (research where-values-come-from). When it lands, snapall's and lab-agent's own completion generators and oco-agent's hand-typed usage retire, and snapall's pinned test turns over: --only becomes a list whose members are asked. 2026-11-13, later the same day: the step designed here is held, not built. Seen from OCO's place (open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, decision 2026-11-13-a-command-line-is-an-entry): what argenv declares is what a lens already declares, and asked is a relation. 2026-11-13, the trial in ocoeco: argenv's reader read a lens entry against records made as the program ran - nothing here had to change. What it showed lacking is not a field: the reader looks one way, taking words in; from a blank, what may enter is not yet answered anywhere but in ocoeco's form, and it needs what only the data knows - which rows exist. 2026-11-14: the trial this waited on has run. Where a value comes from is read off the language and the rows that exist - what fits here, in ocoeco - with nothing in argenv changed (open-commons-observatory/ecosystem, decision 2026-11-13-a-command-line-is-an-entry; open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-14-what-fits-here). What is still so here: a program declared with argenv cannot take a repeated option with free values, nor a list of positionals - that is argenv's own, and no longer waits.
title: Where a value comes from - looked at as one with ocoeco's entries and relations (open question 25)

The first command to build: no risk, it replaces docs' graph-drift.sh (36 FAIL today) and passes it line for line. Edges are read from the pin files followers already own (idealkb.toml, devicebase.toml, lab.toml [tools], a fork's .rhizoid/module.toml), so the follower lists derive from the pins. Rust with argenv, the CLI's status command. Unparked 2026-11-18 (see implement-cli): first in the author's order. Built in rhizoid-cli: status reads a graph file of the edges and each follower's own pin files at origin/main, reports every edge current, behind or moved by hand, exits 1 on drift, and is proven by graph-drift.sh's cases as fixtures and by agreeing with graph-drift.sh run on the real graph. Released 2026-11-18 as git-rhizoid/rhizoid v0.1.0 (PRs 7, 8, 9): rhizoid status over a graph file (examples/linux-phone-oco.graph.toml: slice, device layer, tool pin, fork), agreeing with graph-drift.sh edge by edge on the real graph (tests/agree-with-graph-drift.sh). The graph file exists because idealkb.toml names no source: when pins name theirs (follow-by-conformance, rule one), the follower lists derive from the pins and the file shrinks to what pins cannot say. The graph file for the real graph belongs in linux-phone-oco/docs, whose owner keeps graph-drift.sh. Next: follow-by-conformance.

note: Cause found 2026-11-09 by tracing every request the ADSP makes (a verbose hexagonrpcd build on the phone): the sensors service (hexagonrpcd -s) attaches the ADSP sensor process, whose registry init re-reads the sensor configs and needs to write (temp.json); hexagonrpcd refuses all writes, the firmware asserts (SNS_REG_INIT) and the whole ADSP restarts, taking audio with it. No registry state fixes it (packaged, or the phone own from persist, readable, with the version marker - which hexagonrpcd also never serves: a real gap, patch drafted). Fix in place on the phone: hexagonrpcd-adsp-sensorspd masked. Result: 0 ADSP crashes across three boots and many minutes, the POCO X3 sound card up at about 12 s, playback without crashes. Trade-off: no ADSP sensors, which did not work anyway. Next: propose upstream (do not start sensorspd on surya until registry writes are supported; serve sns_reg_version in hexagonrpcd); see sensors-registry-writes. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed by masking the audio processor's helper services (hexagonrpcd rootpd, sensorspd).
title: The ADSP crashes every 13-25 s, restarting audio each time

note: Trigger found 2026-11-10, one change at a time: with hexagonrpcd's RootPD helper (a FastRPC client) attached, the audio DSP dies on every suspend attempt - 24 of 24 (fatal error EX:kernel:0x0:IST46:0x132:PC=0xf0049be4, about 30 ms after the attempt; the attempts abort at once because the USB link cannot go idle). Without the helper: 0 of 8, and on a clean boot with it masked 0 of 9, all checks passing; sound does not need it. Not a first-boot effect, not the sensor proxy, no stream open. The earlier "rare" crash (2 of 28, both early in a boot) was the same one: there the helper died with the first crashes and stayed down. Fixed in the lab: hexagonrpcd-adsp-rootpd masked in the device manifest, baked in at every flash. Still open, for upstream: why an attached FastRPC client makes the DSP assert across a suspend attempt (the kernel's fastrpc and remoteproc suspend handling, or hexagonrpcd), and why the helper restarts after each crash on a fresh system. Settled 2026-11-11: fixed with the same masks and the awake service.
title: The audio DSP crashes right after resume from suspend

2026-11-17: no longer rare - 3 of 8 boots that night (stock and test kernels alike) came up with the ADSP running but no audio services, so no sound card; restarting remoteproc0 (stop, start) brought the card back each time. The speaker's support is only as good as this; a fix, or at least a recovery at boot, is next after the microphone - or before it if it keeps recurring.

2026-11-17, read from the phone's journal (bring-up): in a bad boot the ADSP comes up but the APR audio services (aprsvc:service:4:3/4/7/8) are never added; in a good boot they appear 0.2 s after 'remote processor adsp is now up'. In the bad boot they appeared only right after the manual ADSP restart. So the protection-domain up notification (PDR, through the in-kernel PD mapper) never arrived. qcom_pd_mapper is a module nothing depends on (lsmod: used by 0), so it can load after the ADSP has booted. Next: load qcom_pd_mapper before the remoteprocs (modules-load.d through the device manifest, or the initramfs), count bad boots over twenty reboots before and after; then the kernel fix (pas depending on the PD mapper) for upstream.

2026-11-17 trial (bring-up): with /etc/modprobe.d/devlab-pd-mapper.conf on the phone (softdep qcom_q6v5_pas pre: qcom_pd_mapper) 13 of 13 boots came up with the sound card, against 8 failing of 42 health runs before. Other distributions do the same (omarchy puts qcom_pd_mapper in the initramfs for Snapdragon laptops). Next: twenty more boots, then carry the file in device.toml's flash overlays with its reason, and the kernel-side fix (the remoteproc driver depending on the PD mapper) for upstream.

Done 2026-11-17 (bring-up): 21 of 21 boots with the sound card since the PD mapper loads before the remoteproc driver; surya's device.toml now carries lab/devlab-pd-mapper.conf to /etc/modprobe.d in every flash. The kernel-side form for upstream is backlog upstream-pd-mapper-order.

note:
Asked for 2026-11-10: the conveyor as a repo of its own, so anyone can bring support to another phone with the same conveyors, CI, tests, tad page and automatic integration into the grand picture; surya is the first instance, not the mould.

Design. (1) linux-phone-oco/device-template, a GitHub template repository: Use this template makes <vendor>-<codename>-lab. (2) device.toml, one manifest per device - codename, SoC, compatible strings, panel variants, image sources, how to reach the phone - read by every script; no script edited per device. (3) Generic machinery, generalized from surya-lab: the phone library (USB or Wi-Fi, commands on stdin), flashing with built-in fixes, provisioning (packages, Wi-Fi from private files), switching shells, device-tree audits, an upstream queue with send commands generated by get_maintainer.pl. (4) Tests as small independent checks, one file each declaring its component and what it needs, so a device runs the checks that apply; results as JSON lines with a versioned schema. (5) Device-independent analysis in linux-phone-oco/lab-tools (Rust): tone (speaker tests microphone) first. (6) Onboarding conveyor: a lab-tools command reads a running phone (compatible, inputs, outputs, sound devices) and fills device.toml - and from the same facts generates the Sxmo device profile. (7) Each device repo publishes its own tad data (support status, test runs, wiki claims) with CI that validates it and renders its page. (8) Integration: a feed in linux-phone-oco/docs discovers device repos by a GitHub topic and pulls their published tables, so a new device appears in the devices table and the support grid (tad draws device x component as a matrix) with no hand edits. (9) Conventions in AGENTS.md: explicit intent for state changes, lists as arguments, secrets outside repos, fingerprints before trusting images. (10) Proof: surya-lab re-based onto the template as its first instance - still 18 of 18 through it. Landscape read 2026-11-10 (see the landscape table): build on what exists - device.toml derives from postmarketOS deviceinfo; tests take the shape of pmOS's initramfs CI tests and use bootrr for driver probes; the lab aims to be a CI-tron-compatible setup and surya a device under test in pmOS's hardware farm; flashing leans on pmbootstrap. 

2026-11-17: made - linux-phone-oco/device-template (a GitHub template): a lab is device.toml, tests/health, tests/results and its records; every tool is devlab's. Proven on surya the same day: the phone checks its own health after every boot (devlab-health, a static Rust runner, generic checks in postmarketOS's test shape, [health] in the manifest, known gaps measured but not ill health), every change devlab makes ends with that report, devlab gather now files the runs here (9 runs filed, a week of filing by hand caught up), devlab mcp is the door for agents. note: Plasma Mobile (fresh Nura image, sound fixes applied on the phone): speakers were silent with the whole chain playing. Two causes, both confirmed: (1) the image restores a saved mixer state with both amplifiers' digital volume at 0 = -110 dB; (2) a tas2562 driver bug: setting the Digital Volume Control changes only the driver's cache, the chips (page 2, 0x0c-0x0f) stay at -110 dB. Writing 0x40000000 straight into both chips with i2cset made sound work: the user heard YouTube in Firefox, 2026-11-10. Not persistent: after a power-off the restore and the driver bug bring the silence back. Needed: the driver fix (upstream-tas2562-volume), and until then a boot-time step that writes the volume into the chips. Root cause found and fixed 2026-11-10: the tas2562 driver's maximum volume (0 dB) read past the end of its lookup table, which muted the amps; with two more faults (the latch byte written first, resume skipping bytes). Fixed module installed and proven on the phone by I2C reads; every flash bakes it in. Listen on Plasma when it is next run.
title: Plasma Mobile: speakers silent, the chain playing

Two tries on 2026-11-11 in the test kernel. The Android route sets cleanly (TX DEC0 MUX=SWR_MIC, TX SMIC MUX0=ADC0, TX_AIF1_CAP Mixer DEC0, ADC1_MIXER, ADC1, MultiMedia2 Mixer TX_CODEC_DMA_TX_3) and the card's routing wires mic bias to AMIC1-3. Starting the capture stream fails: the TX SoundWire bus can no longer read from the codec (read underflow at DPN_PortCtrl of port 1; 'Program transport params failed'), so no recording is made. Not power management: the same with the bus, macros and codec kept awake. Next lead: the moment of failure is when the bus is reshaped for the stream - compare the TX controller's frame and port parameters with the phone's Android kernel. Compared with the Android kernel: the TX bus's port layout and timings match (ports 2-5 as on sm8250 mainline and the vendor), so not the port table. The first read of a port register (DP1 PortCtrl) at stream prepare fails while hundreds of codec register accesses worked at init. Next: trace the bus's transfers (dynamic debug on the SoundWire bus and the qcom controller, or a kernel with SoundWire debugfs - this one has none). Parked 2026-11-12: the lab-agent redesign after the 2026-11-11 incident comes first; resume from the next step above (order: open-commons-observatory decision 2026-11-12-the-redesign-first).

note: Solved 2026-11-11: the audio pin driver muxed gpio19 (TX SoundWire data) to function 1 and gpio23 (RX data) to 3, where the phone's own Android kernel has 3 and 2. With both corrected the TX bus no longer clashes, the codec initialises and the sound card is made with the codec on it. The clocks going to 0 were a consequence, not the cause.
title: The microphone codec times out at initialisation

One distinction held: a place is what says of itself what it is - its mark, the same along every route; a route is a lens; and routes differ in as of when, which a route must not hide (the false alarms about failing runs began there). 2026-11-14: looked at and said - five ways in, three of which said nothing of as of when; and the smallest trial made (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-14-a-route-says-as-of-when): a lens's beam says by which route each table came and as of when. note: 2026-11-13, from the research tables-or-a-graph (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco). Not a move away from tables decided in a head: a trial that lets the commons see whether the graph is already there. What bears on what is written today as text inside rows, taken apart in eight queries and in the program's own code. Gathered once as one relation, a lens could ask what points at a thing, walk from x to g, and say what nothing reaches - and the taking apart would be in one place. What it shows decides the rest: whether facts, not rows, are what is kept; whether identity is what a thing is. Held: text at rest that a person can read and compare is not given up (Logseq's newer form did, and says what it cost). 2026-11-13, the author: as a research prototype on the lab, free of complying with GitHub and git. Looked at beside it: git is itself a content-addressed graph - identity by what a thing is - and GitHub's CI runs any program given it; so what holds us is the shape chosen to write in (rows as lines, a name as an address), and a graph prototype need leave nothing behind - if it proves itself, it can be kept as git objects. The beam (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-13-the-beam) is the first lens over the language's own edges: what a lens reads, what each part places, where it goes on to. 2026-11-14, the trial made (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-14-the-graph-under-the-tables). From the author's observatory: 2,362 things, 1,516 links between them, every link holding, in 0.3 s. What it showed, unasked: the most pointed-at thing is lab-agent's safety-first, 46 times; 1,748 things - three in four - have nothing pointing at them, most by their nature (records of work, runs, translations, connections: what flows in one direction and ends at a surface), and some not (125 of 329 items, 82 of 198 decisions, 122 of 138 concepts, 35 of 39 practices); the longest line of answers is the author's own conversation, reflection answering reflection sixteen deep; ten decisions refine one another in a line; and repeats comes back to where it began - a group, not a line. Not yet: the eight parts that take a name apart still do so, and the program still checks links on its own - both now have the graph to read instead. 2026-11-14: six parts that took a written link apart now read the graph, and work, signs and purpose show what they showed, line for line, over every place (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-14-lenses-read-the-graph). Left: the check still finds what points nowhere on its own; a condition told by tests is not an edge; and one shape asked twice in purpose, now seen - what is lacking is a shape one part names and another asks of: a projection that feeds a lens. 2026-11-14: shapes pass between lenses (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-14-shapes-across-lenses). The graph names what points nowhere; the lens of signs asks of it and shows it as a sign. Tried in a copy of this place with one link made to point nowhere: the lens of signs showed it through the graph's shape, and the check said the same on its own - the one meaning still kept twice, now between a lens and the program. Next: the check reads the shape. 2026-11-14: done: every link in view is one relation - this, how, that - with the nature of its pointing; the check, the lenses and what fits read it; the language itself is in it; one stands on any thing and walks.
title: The graph under the tables: every link in the commons as one relation - this, how, that - read by any lens

Looked at by hand first: nine lenses hold 17 tables, 124 fields, 16 relations, 13 entries, 34 parts in focus. id is declared in every table; by and date in four or five, though every entry already says the computer supplies who and when; one query is written three times inside one lens. As rows, a field declared in five tables, two parts asking the same thing, a table nothing brings into focus are signs shown while true. It shows; whoever sees merges - the tool does not merge by itself. Reasoned, to be measured by it: three records of something done are kept apart - records of work, the lab's journal of jobs, and observed runs. 2026-11-13, made: the lens of language (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-13-the-language-looks-at-itself). note: Today the lens holds a problem and a countermeasure in prose. To become: a sign with its kind (stale, overlapping, lacking, unclear) and where it points; ended by a link to what changed the whole. Signs that are derived stay as they are - they are already this: shown while true, gone when the whole fits. The four things the week's seventeen point at are the first to take up: a change on the lab as one act; what is observed kept apart from where work lands; readiness named as the rung it is; a link chosen among what exists rather than typed. 2026-11-13, the author: what a connection says in prose can be entered as intelligible data - relations between a need, a decision made to fill another need, a need that fills a gap, a need that clarifies an overlap; and a need in general always seems to be a need for clarity. So three things kept apart are one with different faces: a sign with its kind (stale, overlapping, lacking, unclear) is how a need shows; X needed Y is a need named between two things; a milestone ahead is a need met, praised. What was written as three records and a practice being one sign was the need those signs point at. It becomes one piece of work with milestones-read-off-the-data. Held to the test used so far: a row is made where something is then read off it; where nothing would be, words stay. 2026-11-13, the author, setting a phrase right: a whole is not changing - a whole is always a whole; we discover it, how what is in it fits together; and what is lacking, a gap, is something we do not yet see in the whole and how it relates inside it. So a need is not met by what changed the whole, as was written here, but when what was lacking is seen. 2026-11-13, the first half made (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-13-the-lens-of-signs): the lens speaks of signs, asks what, where and what kind, and a sign stops being shown when a connection leads from it - no table added, nothing asked about what was done. Laid side by side first: that one thing needs another was written five ways, two of them sentences. Left: a milestone ahead shown from what is halted or needed; waits_on as something that can be followed; and the same line about work that has not moved, still asked by two lenses.
title: Signs, needs and milestones as one: a sign points at a need; a need is met when what was lacking is seen, and how it fits; a milestone is that, praised

note: 2026-11-13, from the lens of language. Three signs to look at as what they are, not to counter one by one: at and date are both when this was written; the problems lens and the work lens each decide what stalled means; manual_events is defined and filled and never shown. And one reasoned, for the lens to measure: three records of something done - records of work, the lab's journal of jobs, observed runs - are kept apart. 2026-11-13, the author's glimpse: what leads to no interface dissolves, like the natural rotation of things in an ecosystem. Rhizome's own words: a changed thing is a different thing, and the original still exists, unchanged, forever - it does not say what lets go. Here the first such thing was shown the first time the language looked: a table nothing brings into focus. The same can be asked of rows - of the board's 169 open items, how many serve nothing, were advanced by no work and are touched by no connection is not known, and until this week could not be asked. Held beside it: what is not shown today is sometimes the why someone needs later, so being pointed at counts, not only being shown; and what is scarce here is not the disk but what a person or an agent must carry in view - so dissolving is fading from view while nothing reaches a thing, and its coming back when something does. 2026-11-13, one of its signs came to something: what has not moved for more than seven days was asked by two lenses; the work lens now places that part of the lens of signs (open-commons-observatory/ocoeco, decision 2026-11-13-a-lens-of-lenses), and the lens of language no longer finds the line twice - nobody cleared it.

note: The commons' rule is a declared command line (argenv). ocoeco still uses clap; the entries of lenses are checked for collisions by the build script. When ocoeco moves to argenv, each entry's flags become part of the declared contract. 2026-11-13: the most valuable of the five to move. Lens entries are taken before the parser by hand, because the older library could not take what lenses declare; with argenv a build step makes the declarations from the lens files, so entries are real commands with help, completions and man pages, and a collision is the compiler's to find. 2026-11-13, looked at what argenv carries: typed inputs (text, yes or no, one of a set, a list, numbers, a path), options that repeat, positionals, inputs scoped to one command, and usage and a schema made from the one declaration. Nothing ocoeco needs is missing for the move; only offering the id of an existing row waits on argenv's own open item (a list known only at runtime). The author has set this first: the fulldome's form tells how to use it from a legend typed by hand - a program dictating its use from behind brackets. 2026-11-13, set right: it was said here that nothing ocoeco needs is missing in argenv. That was read off the names of its fields, not tried. Tried: a repeated option with free values, and more positionals than are named, cannot be declared. The need is met in argenv, where it lives, before ocoeco moves. 2026-11-13, the trial (a throwaway program, nothing changed in either repository): the item entry of the work lens, turned into records as the program runs, was read by argenv's own reader as it is. Three signs: needed is not one thing (a title is needed for a new row, not for a change - known only from what exists, and a record can only say always); the reader cannot say a link points nowhere (what a relation knows has nowhere to go in a record); and it reads what was typed but does not say what could be.
